articles.title: Do the Math
articles.summary: This article emphasizes the importance of basic mathematical concepts for understanding astronomy, even for those who typically dislike math. It explains five fundamental formulas: the Kelvin scale for absolute temperature, Wien's Law to relate temperature to peak emission wavelength, Kepler's 3rd Law for planetary orbits, the Distance Modulus to calculate celestial distances, and Telescope Magnification.

articles.title: The Shallow Sky
articles.summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide for observing Mars throughout February, detailing various surface features visible at different times, such as the "Eye of Mars," Syrtis Major, and Hellas. It encourages amateur astronomers to use high power and sketching techniques to explore the planet's dynamic appearance, noting its favorable high altitude post-opposition. The author also briefly mentions Saturn and offers an update on the Mars Spirit rover.

articles.title: Sunglasses for a Solar Observatory
articles.summary: A powerful solar flare in 2006 damaged the Solar X-Ray Imager (SXI) on NOAA's GOES-13 satellite, highlighting the challenge of monitoring intense solar events without sensor overexposure. In response, NASA engineers developed new flight-software "sunglasses" for the GOES-14 satellite. This innovation allows its SXI sensor to safely observe even extreme solar flares through five graduated levels of protection, balancing data collection with crucial sensor safety for space weather forecasting.

articles.title: Hubble Ultra Deep Field - Infrared and other notes
articles.summary: This article highlights the new Hubble Ultra Deep Field infrared image, captured by the rehabbed Hubble Space Telescope's WFC3/IR instrument, revealing galaxies 13 billion years distant and intrinsically blue. It also includes a Q&A about supernova progenitor candidates and features local news for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), such as upcoming board elections and information about their telescope loaner program.

articles.title: The Last Month In Astronomy
articles.summary: This article, summarizing 'The Last Month In Astronomy' (late 2009 - early 2010), highlights significant advancements including the discovery of new exoplanets by Keck and Kepler, and updated estimates on the prevalence of Earth-like planets. Key space missions saw milestones with ALMA linking antennae, WISE launching for an infrared sky map, and Cassini confirming liquid hydrocarbons on Titan. Additionally, NASA selected finalists for future unmanned missions, and astronaut John Grunsfeld took a leadership role at STScI.
